text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Household consumption of manufactured goods fell 1.5 percent in September, but economists expect a good performance over the year.
-- SNCF rail operator registered a 7.5-billion-franc loss in the first half.

-- Giat Industries arms manufacturer chairman Jacques Loppion says in an interview firm expects to post a loss of 1.3 billion francs for 1996 and considers raising the price of its Leclerc assault tank.

-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis defends government plans to privatise Thomson on grounds that its finances showed a 6.9 billion francs negative balance, but sale to Lagardere Groupe for one symbolic franc is widely criticised, notably by CFDT union which claims Thomson could have been sold for nine to 14 billion francs.

-- Government expects Social Security regime to post a 12.3 billion francs loss in 1998, return to the black in 1999 on back of an expected pickup of economic growth and health spending control. Forecast for 1997 is a 29.7 billion franc loss.
-- Blue-chip CAC 40 index closed on a 4.09 percent rise at Paris bourse yesterday, due to firms' good first-half results and expectations of further rate cuts.
-- Workers of Credit Lyonnais and CIC ailing state-owned banks to demonstrate today for jobs.
-- Government report says civil servants' wages are on average six percent higher than those of their private sector counterparts.
-- Government studies plan to boost purchasing power for lower income households through refunds on savings plans.
-- Banques Populaires tipped to buy a 50 percent stake in Credit du Nord, a Paribas subsidiary.

-- French firms call for tighter rules to protect them against hostile takeovers from abroad, but report finds firms are chronically undercapitalized and inefficiently run, making them easier targets.
